source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with influenza is recovering at home. Which finding should prompt referral for possible pneumonia?
questions.rationale: The nurse watches for developing pneumonia: crackles, another temperature rise, or coughing with purulent or bloody sputum.
questions.quote: Watch for signs and symptoms of developing pneumonia such as crackles, another temperature increase

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A farmer who butchered a sick carabao has a painless sore with a black scab and purplish vesicles. Which disease is suspected?
questions.rationale: Cutaneous anthrax, over 90% of cases, starts as a pimple that ulcerates and forms a black scab surrounded by purplish vesicles. It comes from contact with tissues of animals dying of the disease.
questions.quote: grows, ulcerates and forms a black scab, around which are purplish vesicles

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hand hygiene is needed after caring for a client with anthrax?
questions.rationale: Alcohol-based hand sanitizers do not kill anthrax spores, so hands are washed with soap and water.
questions.quote: Alcohol-based hand sanitizers do not kill anthrax spores; wash hands with soap and water.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which form of anthrax is the MOST fatal?
questions.rationale: Inhalational anthrax begins abruptly like the flu, then causes dyspnea, cyanosis, shock, and usually death in 2–6 days.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Before starting antibiotics for suspected anthrax, what should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Culture specimens are obtained before antibiotic therapy starts.
questions.quote: Obtain culture specimens before starting antibiotic therapy

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which sputum characteristic is classic for pneumococcal pneumonia?
questions.rationale: Pneumococcal pneumonia causes productive cough with rusty sputum, high fever, chest pain, and dullness on percussion over the affected lobe.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Rudy, 52, a tricycle driver, has had a cough for 3 weeks with afternoon fevers and night sweats.
questions.stem: Which test CONFIRMS pulmonary TB in Mang Rudy?
questions.rationale: Sputum analysis for AFB is confirmatory. Tuberculin tests show exposure, and a chest X-ray supports the diagnosis.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Mang Rudy, 52, a tricycle driver, has had a cough for 3 weeks with afternoon fevers and night sweats.
questions.stem: Mang Rudy will take isoniazid. Which supplement should the nurse encourage?
questions.rationale: Isoniazid can cause peripheral neuropathy, so vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) intake is increased. Alcohol is avoided because of hepatotoxicity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis – Isoniazid (PDF p. 161)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Rudy, 52, a tricycle driver, has had a cough for 3 weeks with afternoon fevers and night sweats.
questions.stem: Mang Rudy develops joint pain on pyrazinamide. Which lab result should the nurse check?
questions.rationale: Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricemia and can be hepatotoxic, so uric acid and liver function are monitored.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis – Pyrazinamide (PDF p. 161)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A woman starting rifampicin for TB uses oral contraceptives. What should the nurse teach?
options: The pill may be less effective
Stop TB drugs on pill days
questions.rationale: Rifampin can make oral contraceptives less effective, so a backup method is advised.
questions.quote: Caution the patient who is taking an oral contraceptive that the contraceptive may be less effective while she’s taking rifampin.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the main purpose of DOTS in TB control?
questions.rationale: Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course is a strategy to prevent non-compliance by having a treatment partner watch the client take each dose.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which TB drug should be AVOIDED in children under 6 because of optic neuritis?
questions.rationale: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis and is not recommended for children below 6, who cannot reliably report visual changes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis – Ethambutol (PDF p. 161)
questions.quote: Not recommended for children (below 6 years old); can cause optic neuritis

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Bird flu is found in a poultry farm. Which control measure is used?
options: Cull birds and disinfect the farm
questions.rationale: Control includes rapid destruction and proper disposal of birds, quarantine and rigorous disinfection of farms, and restrictions on moving live poultry.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bird Flu (PDF p. 162)
questions.quote: Rapid destruction, proper disposal of carcasses and quarantining and rigorous disinfection of farms

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the initial sign of SARS?
questions.rationale: The prodromal phase of SARS begins with fever above 38°C, then chills, malaise, myalgia, and headache. A dry cough follows.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: After a flood, a barangay reports many cases of profuse diarrhea.
questions.stem: A client passes stools that look like rice water and has wrinkled fingertips. Which disease is suspected?
questions.rationale: Cholera causes profuse rice-watery stool and 'washer-woman's hands' from severe dehydration, which can lead to hypovolemic shock.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: After a flood, a barangay reports many cases of profuse diarrhea.
questions.stem: What is the incubation period of cholera?
questions.rationale: Cholera has a short incubation period of 6 to 48 hours. Cases are infectious during diarrhea and up to 7 days after.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: After a flood, a barangay reports many cases of profuse diarrhea.
questions.stem: Which isolation is used for a hospitalized client with cholera?
questions.rationale: Cholera spreads through feces and vomitus, so enteric isolation with handwashing and accurate I&O is used.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Typhoid fever is characterized by ulceration of which tissue?
questions.rationale: Typhoid fever is a systemic Salmonella typhi infection with continued fever, anorexia, and involvement of lymphoid tissue, especially ulceration of Peyer's patches.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Typhoid Fever (PDF p. 164)
